## Natural history notes

A crustose lichen characterized by a thin gray to greenish-gray thallus with dark, smudgy, comma-like fruiting marks scattered across the surface. In Florida, it is found growing on palm trunks and other bark surfaces in humid habitats such as hammocks, swamps, mangroves, shaded forests, parks, and landscaped areas where suitable host bark is available. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, growing tightly attached to bark and absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on the tree itself.
